lines: This is a real tank, measured with a stereo camera. And this is a dream of it, made by a video model from one photograph.
The real side isn't a recording. It's the tank rebuilt from stereo, and seen again from wherever the dream's camera goes.
Grey is where no real camera ever looked. There, nothing can be checked, and the page says so.
The heat shows where the dream's tank disagrees with the real one. Orange is too near. Blue is too far.
The scrubber is the score. A D of one is no worse than measuring the real tank. At three, the tank has changed shape.
Here, just under four seconds in, the far wall opens into a corridor that isn't there. Every pixel is still checkable. Only the depth gives it away.
Across thirty-five clips, three leave the tank for good. And the dreams don't fill the tank. They open it up.
If video models are going to make worlds, test them against a measured place, frame by frame, and say where you can no longer check.
